Koridori Srbije d.o.o..desc: A Serbian limited liability company set up in 2009 to act as the investor on motorway building: it organises the works, runs international tenders, carries out expropriation and prepares project documentation. The Ministry of Economy's list of state-owned capital companies (Official Gazette 77/2024 and 97/2025) names "Koridori Srbije" d.o.o. Belgrade among companies in majority state ownership, in the category of national and strategic interest. Its own status report of 3 October 2013 names four responsible ministries (Transport, Finance, Construction and Regional Development), 104 employees, projects totalling EUR 1.4 billion in loans and donations, and works then under way on 129.7 km at 167 locations on Corridors 10 and 11.

sources.title: Koridori Srbije doo, status overview presented at Danube Region Transport Days (Belgrade)

Public Enterprise Roads of Serbia.desc: The Serbian state body that manages the state road network: collecting road-use charges, investing in road building and reconstruction, maintenance, planning and traffic management. It was set up by a Government of Serbia decision of 22 December 2005 (05 no. 023/8228/2005) that took effect on 1 January 2006, with the Republic of Serbia as founder and its seat in Belgrade. In December 2025 the government adopted a decision, published in the Official Gazette, changing the legal form of Putevi Srbije and six other public enterprises to limited liability companies; the reports of it give no effective date.

Seven Public Enterprises Becoming Limited Companies
Posta, Putevi Srbije i jos nekoliko javnih preduzeca zvanicno prelaze u d.o.o.

General Roads Directorate.desc: Albania's national road agency. The state audit office's 2016 audit of it describes it programming and implementing road investments, procuring and contracting road studies, design and supervision, procuring and supervising construction works, running a technical council that approves terms of reference, cost estimates and design changes, submitting expropriation requests to the Council of Ministers, and keeping the road inventory it reports to the transport ministry. The same report calls the General Roads Directorate (Drejtoria e Pergjithshme e Rrugeve) "sot Autoriteti Rrugor Shqiptar" - today the Albanian Road Authority, which operates under Law no. 10164 of 15 October 2009 - without giving the date of the change.

Ministry of Public Works and Housing.desc: Jordan's public works ministry. It builds, develops and maintains the national road network linking cities, villages, housing, industrial and farming areas and neighbouring countries, prepares plans and designs for public, village and agricultural roads, designs and supervises government buildings, runs laboratory testing of construction materials for quality control, and drafts building and road legislation. The government portal traces it to the "Al Naf'a" department set up with the Emirate of East Jordan in 1923, attached to the transport ministry in 1939 and named the Ministry of Public Works in 1954.

sources.title: Ministry of Public Works and Housing - General Information

Department of Lands and Surveys.desc: Jordan's land registry and survey department. Under clause 3 of its administrative organisation bylaw no. 80 of 1999 it surveys the country's land and fixes boundaries, issues cadastral maps, registers and maintains property rights, values land for registration, administers and leases treasury land, handles land taken for the public interest, and licenses surveyors and land agents; it also keeps the national land information base. Its own history page traces it to the Ottoman Land Law of 1857 and records the merger of the East and West Bank land departments in 1951-52. Neither page names the ministry it sits under.

sources.title: Department of Lands and Survey - General Information
The Historical Development of the Department

Cameroon Railways (CAMRAIL).desc: The sole concessionaire of Cameroon's railway, carrying passengers and freight along the 918 km Transcamerounais line, with much of the freight coming from Chad and the Central African Republic. It took over the state railway Regifercam in the 1999 privatisation, was a subsidiary of France's Bollore group and has since passed to Africa Global Logistics. At a February 2025 business meeting the company said it pays about 10 billion FCFA (USD 16 million) a year in taxes and levies and invests close to 12 billion FCFA a year; no year is given for either figure.

sources.title: Cameroun: Camrail declare le paiement de 16 millions USD d'impots par an

Hohai University.desc: A Chinese university founded in 1915 and under the direct administration of China's Ministry of Education, specialising in water conservancy research and engineering education and also teaching science, economics, management, liberal arts and law. Its own international school page, last updated in January 2015, gave 3,409 faculty, 46,921 students and 19 colleges and departments.

sources.title: About Hohai University

National Directorate for Water Resources.desc: A national directorate of Mozambique's Ministry of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources, listed as one of the ministry's units in article 7(a) of Ministerial Diploma no. 12/2022 of 25 January 2022. Article 9 gives it nineteen functions, among them ensuring water is available in sufficient quantity and quality for different uses, preparing and monitoring river-basin plans, and keeping hydraulic infrastructure maintained. It works through four departments: water resources management, hydraulic works, international water resources and strategic studies.

sources.title: Diploma Ministerial n. 12/2022, Regulamento Interno do Ministerio das Obras Publicas, Habitacao e Recursos Hidricos (arts. 7 and 9)

Energoinvest.desc: A Sarajevo-based engineering company established in 1951 that designs, supplies and builds substations, transmission lines, thermal and hydro power plants and water and wastewater works on a turnkey basis, mostly as an exporter and lately in Africa, the Middle East and southeast Europe. A 2021 report on its seventieth anniversary says the government still held 67% of its shares and that it had been slated for possible privatisation; it does not say which level of government. The same report says the company employed more than 54,000 people before the Yugoslav war.

sources.title: Yugoslavia 30 years on: seven decades of Bosnia's red capitalist Energoinvest
Energoinvest d.d. Sarajevo - company and services

Ethiopian Electric Power Corporation (EE.desc: Ethiopia's state-run electricity monopoly, which generated, transmitted and distributed the country's power. It no longer exists as a single body: an Addis Standard report says the government split the corporation in two, and its successors were set up by Ethiopian Electric Power Establishment Regulation No. 302/2013, which implements power projects and runs the national grid, and Ethiopian Electric Utility Establishment Regulation No. 303/2013, which handles distribution and retail supply (both amended in 2016). The report naming the split prints no date on the page.

Secretaria dos Recursos Hidricos do Cear.desc: A secretariat of the direct state administration of Ceara, Brazil, created by state Law no. 11,306 of 1 April 1987. It carries out the state water resources policy in an integrated, decentralised and participatory way, coordinates studies, programmes and works on water resources, and links state bodies in the sector with federal and municipal ones; its structure was set by state Decree no. 32,957 of 13 February 2019 and regulated by Decree no. 33,215 of 19 August 2019.

sources.title: Sintese do Primeiro Ciclo do Progestao no Ceara (2014-2018)

Superintendencia de Obras Hidraulicas (S.desc: The state of Ceara's hydraulic works agency (Brazil): the body that builds the works. The project completion report's acronym list expands it as "Superintendencia de Obras Hidraulicas do Ceara - Hydraulic Works Company" and its paragraph 943 calls it "an agency responsible for construction of hydraulic works". It is part of the water-sector structure the state set up in 1987 and "vinculada" to the state water resources secretariat (SRH), and it builds and supervises dams, integration axes, canals, pipelines, wells and water supply systems, including small water works.

sources.title: Sintese do Primeiro Ciclo do Progestao no Ceara (2014-2018)
Implementation Completion and Results Report, Ceara Integrated Water Resources Management Project (P006449), acronym list and para. 943

National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG).desc: An Indian government body: a society registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860 which the River Ganga (Rejuvenation, Protection and Management) Authorities Order of 10 July 2016 also makes an authority under the Environment (Protection) Act 1986. The Order makes it the nodal agency for implementing the Order nationwide, requires it to prepare the Ganga basin management plan and to notify ecological flows, and lets it issue directions to state and district Ganga committees and local authorities. Its Director General is appointed by the central government at the rank of Additional Secretary or Secretary, and its accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General.

sources.title: River Ganga (Rejuvenation, Protection and Management) Authorities Order, 2016 (ss. 31-47)

Office National de l'Eau et de l'Assaini.desc: Burkina Faso's national water and sanitation office, created by Decree no. 85-387 of 22 July 1985 and turned into a state company (societe d'Etat) by Decree no. 94-391 of 2 November 1994. Since 1 July 2001 it has held a 40-year public service concession to operate the Ziga dam, whose water is reserved for supplying Ouagadougou and nearby localities, for a symbolic fee of 1 FCFA; it carries out the dam's routine upkeep, while major repairs affecting the dam's stability and safety remain the State's responsibility.

sources.title: Decret n. 2003-113/PRES/PM/MAHRH/MFB portant concession de service public pour l'exploitation du barrage de Ziga

Department of Local Infrastructure Devel.desc: A department of the Government of Nepal responsible for local infrastructure: it implements agricultural and rural road programmes and plans, monitors and evaluates local roads, irrigation, water supply, bridges, housing and rural energy, sets norms, standards and manuals for them, and gives local authorities resource maps, technical studies and training. Its own older pages place these duties within the Ministry of Local Development; its site now publishes as the Department of Local Infrastructure (DoLI) under the Ministry of Urban Development, with a Local Infrastructure Development Program Office for Bagmati province under it. No page opened gives an instrument for the change of name or ministry.
